headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

Below is a quick‑start guide to a **ready‑made API** that accepts an IP address and returns the owning company (or ISP) along with any available contact information. If you prefer to build your own service, I’ll also outline the steps and data sources you’d need. --- ## 1. Ready‑made API Options | Service | Endpoint | Key Features | Free Tier | Typical Response | |---------|----------|--------------|-----------|------------------| | **ipinfo.io** | `https://ipinfo.io//json` | • Company name, ASN, carrier
• Contact email & phone (if provided)
• City, region, country, postal code | 50 k requests/month | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","hostname":"dns.google","city":"Mountain View","region":"California","country":"US","loc":"37.3860,-122.0840","org":"AS15169 Google LLC","postal":"94035","timezone":"America/Los_Angeles","readme":"https://ipinfo.io/missingauth"} ``` | | **ipstack.com** | `https://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=YOUR_KEY` | • Company name, ISP, organization
• Contact email & phone (paid tier)
• Geo‑location, currency, languages | 10 k requests/month | ```json{ "ip":"134.201.250.155","type":"ipv4","continent_code":"NA","continent_name":"North America","country_code":"US","country_name":"United States","region_code":"CA","region_name":"California","city":"Los Angeles","zip":"90012","latitude":34.0453,"longitude":-118.2519,"location":{"geoname_id":5368361,"capital":"Washington D.C.","languages":[{"code":"en","name":"English","native":"English"}],"country_flag":"https://assets.ipstack.com/flags/us.svg","country_flag_emoji":"🇺🇸","country_flag_emoji_unicode":"U+1F1FA U+1F1F8","calling_code":"1","is_eu":false},"time_zone":{"id":"America/Los_Angeles","current_time":"2024-06-23T12:34:56-07:00","gmt_offset":-25200,"gmt_offset_name":"GMT-07:00","short_name":"PDT","time":"2024-06-23T12:34:56-07:00"},"currency":{"code":"USD","name":"United States Dollar","symbol":"$"},"connection":{"asn":15169,"isp":"Google LLC","organization":"Google LLC","domain":"google.com","mobile":false,"proxy":false,"tor":false,"vpn":false},"security":{"threat":false,"risk":false,"proxy":false,"tor":false,"vpn":false}} ``` | | **ipapi.co** | `https://ipapi.co//json/` | • Company name, ISP, organization
• Contact email & phone (paid tier)
• Geo‑location, currency, languages | 30 k requests/month | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","city":"Mountain View","region":"California","region_code":"CA","country":"US","country_name":"United States","country_code_iso2":"US","country_code_iso3":"USA","country_capital":"Washington","country_tld":".us","continent_code":"NA","in_eu":false,"postal":"94035","latitude":37.386,"longitude":-122.0838,"timezone":"America/Los_Angeles","utc_offset":"+01:00","country_calling_code":"+1","currency":"USD","languages":"en-US,es-US","asn":"AS15169","org":"Google LLC","ip_version":"IPv4","ip_type":"public","mobile":false,"proxy":false,"hosting":false} ``` | ### How to Use (Example with `ipinfo.io`) ```bash # Replace with the target IP address curl https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json ``` If you need contact details (email, phone) you’ll usually have to upgrade to a paid plan; most free tiers only return the company/ISP name. --- ## 2. Building Your Own IP‑to‑Company Service If you want full control (e.g., no rate limits, custom fields, or offline usage), you can assemble your own database: 1. **Acquire IP‑range → Organization mappings** * **ARIN / RIPE / APNIC** – Each Regional Internet Registry publishes a WHOIS database. * **Team Cymru IP to ASN Mapping** – `https://www.team-cymru.com/ip-to-asn.html` (free CSV). * **IP2Location LITE** – Free database with ISP and organization names. 2. **Parse the data** * Convert CIDR blocks into a searchable structure (e.g., a radix tree or a PostgreSQL `inet` column). * Store fields: `ip_range`, `asn`, `org_name`, `contact_email`, `contact_phone`, `website`, `country`. 3. **Create a REST endpoint** ```python # Flask example from flask import Flask, jsonify, request import ipaddress app = Flask(__name__) @app.route('/lookup/') def lookup(ip): # Convert to int for fast lookup ip_int = int(ipaddress.IPv4Address(ip)) # Query your DB (pseudo‑code) record = db.query("SELECT * FROM ip_orgs WHERE start <= ? AND end >= ?", (ip_int, ip_int)).first() if record: return jsonify(record.to_dict()) return jsonify({"error":"Not found"}), 404 ``` 4. **Populate contact info** * Scrape company websites or use public APIs (e.g., Hunter.io, Clearbit) to fetch emails/phones. * Store only what you’re legally allowed to keep (GDPR, CCPA). 5. **Deploy** * Containerize with Docker, expose via HTTPS, add caching (Redis) for speed. ### Pros & Cons | Pros | Cons | |------|------| | Unlimited requests, no external quota | Requires maintenance of IP ranges (updates every ~30 days) | | Full control over data fields | Initial data ingestion can be heavy | | No cost after initial setup | Must handle privacy compliance | --- ## 3. Quick‑Start Code Snippet (Python + `requests`) ```python import requests def get_company_info(ip, api_key=None): """ Uses ipinfo.io to fetch company data for an IP. """ url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json" headers = {"Accept": "application/json"} if api_key: url += f"?token={api_key}" resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() data = resp.json() # Extract useful fields return { "ip": data.get("ip"), "company": data.get("org"), "city": data.get("city"), "region": data.get("region"), "country": data.get("country"), "postal": data.get("postal"), "timezone": data.get("timezone"), # ipinfo.io does not expose email/phone in free tier } print(get_company_info("8.8.8.8", api_key="YOUR_TOKEN")) ``` --- ## 4. Things to Keep in Mind | Topic | Recommendation | |-------|----------------| | **Rate limits** | Check the provider’s limits; consider caching results. | | **Privacy** | Do not store personal data without consent. | | **Accuracy** | IP ownership can change; keep your database updated. | | **Legal** | Verify that your use case complies with local data‑protection laws. | --- ### Bottom line *If you just need a quick, reliable lookup, start with **ipinfo.io** or **ipapi.co**—they’re simple to call and already contain company/ISP data.* *If you need unlimited requests, custom fields, or offline access, build your own service using the public WHOIS databases and a lightweight lookup engine.*
